resources.string: Fall back to compatible link

Some older phones stop accepting the fast Bluetooth LE (L2CAP) link after about 15 uses, until Bluetooth is restarted. With this on, when L2CAP stops working this phone moves its calls to the slower, more compatible GATT link and tells you. Phones that already use GATT also appear in your call list. It only matters if you chose the L2CAP link under Advanced.
Listen on both links
Accept calls over both Bluetooth LE connection types, and retry with the more compatible connection if needed. Applies when L2CAP is selected under Advanced.
Classic Bluetooth without pairing

Classic Bluetooth calls and streams work without pairing the phones in Android settings. The app\'s own signed handshake and encryption protect the link. Turn it on in both phones. A first call to a phone this one has not met needs that phone to be visible to nearby Bluetooth devices for about two minutes; Android asks before it does that.
Connect without pairing

When this is on, a phone that is ready for Classic calls may ask Android to make it visible to nearby Bluetooth devices for two minutes, so another phone can find it the first time. While it is visible, anyone nearby can see its Bluetooth name. Android always asks you first, and the app still authenticates every connection.\n\nBoth phones need this turned on. Streams reach only phones this one has already met.
Turn on
Find iPhones

Also look for the short announcement an iPhone sends while its MeshLive app is open, so iPhone callers, viewers and streams appear in the lists. Searching uses one more scan filter. An iPhone whose app is in the background cannot be found. Your own announcement and every security check stay the same.
Find PCs (experimental)
PC live streams (experimental)

With Find PCs on, let computers join your live stream and show live streams from computers. Needs a phone that can receive longer Bluetooth announcements. Identity checks and encryption stay the same.

Also look for the short announcement a Windows PC sends, so a PC that runs MeshLive can appear in the call list. Searching uses one more scan filter and also listens for longer adverts, and works only on a phone whose Bluetooth supports them. Needs rotating call IDs to be on. Your own announcement and every security check stay the same.
Show Share app nearby in Help

Adds Share app nearby to Help. This phone starts its own Wi-Fi Direct network and a download page, and shows two codes another phone scans to join it and download the app without internet. It stops after 10 minutes, and it cannot start during a stream or call because Wi-Fi Direct slows Bluetooth.
Call audio with loss recovery

Calls use the Opus speech codec built into the app, set for voice, with error correction and concealment when packets are lost. The other phone needs nothing new. It uses a little more processor time, and calls fall back to the phone\'s own codec if the library cannot start. Applies to calls started after you change it.
Hide my ID from strangers

Adds privacy protection when connecting to other phones. Older versions or phones with this protection turned off may not connect. Accepting a call can still let the other person recognise your phone.
New identity for each stranger

Uses a temporary ID with people you haven\'t verified. Verified contacts, and whoever holds a call you accept (which may be a relaying phone), receive your usual ID. Both phones need compatible settings. Message exchanges require verified contacts. Live streams are not covered: while you send, watch or pass on a stream, anyone nearby with radio equipment can record your usual ID.
You can verify this person once they have answered and their identity is confirmed.
Wi-Fi
Use Wi-Fi when it helps

When both phones support it, calls and live streams move to Wi-Fi after they connect. Bluetooth still finds and connects, and takes over if Wi-Fi stops. Turned on during a call or live stream, it works from the next one. While a call or stream moves to Wi-Fi, both phones briefly advertise a one-time Wi-Fi name. While a Wi-Fi link is open, the other phone can reach other apps on this phone that accept network connections from any network. On a live stream that other phone can be any stranger who watches your stream or whose stream you watch, so keep this off when you stream with people you do not know. While it is on, anyone listening near a live stream you take part in, and the phones next to this one when it relays a call, can see which MeshLive version you use.
On this Android version it also needs Wider reach.
Wider reach over Wi-Fi

Also finds and connects to people over Wi-Fi, further away and faster, even when Bluetooth is blocked. Uses more battery. Nearby Wi-Fi devices can see that this phone uses Wi-Fi Aware. Its Wi-Fi name changes at least every 30 minutes; while a Wi-Fi link is open, its Wi-Fi address may not change. Any nearby phone can open a Wi-Fi link to it before proving who it is, and while a Wi-Fi link is open the other phone can reach other apps on this phone that accept network connections from any network.
Wi-Fi Direct for phones and PCs without Wi-Fi Aware

Lets this phone connect over Wi-Fi Direct. Nearby devices can see this phone\'s Wi-Fi Direct name \"%1$s\" and may recognise it across calls by its Wi-Fi Direct address. While a Wi-Fi Direct link is open, its network name has a pattern that identifies MeshLive, and a nearby device can send this phone an invitation to connect. While a Wi-Fi link is open, the other phone can reach other apps on this phone that accept network connections from any network.

While a Wi-Fi Direct link is open, its network name has a pattern that identifies MeshLive, and a nearby device can send this phone an invitation to connect. While a Wi-Fi link is open, the other phone can reach other apps on this phone that accept network connections from any network.

Precise location is needed. On this Android version, Wi-Fi discovery works only with precise location; the app never reads where you are. The Wi-Fi option stays off. You can allow it in this app\'s settings.

Turn on Wi-Fi Direct?

When a call can use Wi-Fi Direct, this phone and the other phone briefly set up a small Wi-Fi network of their own. Phones nearby can see this phone as \"%1$s\" (its Wi-Fi Direct name) and may recognise it from one call to the next. While the link is open, the other phone can reach other apps on this phone that accept network connections. Bluetooth stays as the backup.
